journal.text: You wake in the lock house. The town has been silent for three days. On the kitchen table, the note Mr Orme left that night.
You find something written: Note on the kitchen table.
You drop the night line from the lock gate, unbaited.
Workbench: Workbench. Snares, picks, a satchel.
You drink the clean water.
You fill 2 measures from the lock. Brown water. Boil it.
You lay out what to take to Towpath Cottages.
You set out for Towpath Cottages.
Towpath Cottages. A row of six on the towpath. Most doors are open.
Two chairs turned to a cold grate. The clock on the mantel has stopped at ten past two.
You go through the room slowly. You find candle x2, chocolate x2, cloth x5 and planks x2.
You find a photograph: Wedding, chapel steps.
You take chocolate x2.
You take candle x2.
You take cloth x5.
You take planks x2.
A pan on the range, a crust of something in it. Plates set for two.
You go through the room slowly. You find ship's biscuit, kitchen knife, oats x2, tea leaves, tinned meat x2 and clean water.
You find something written: Appointment card.
Now you know where to find The Surgery.
You take ship's biscuit.
You take kitchen knife.
You take tinned meat x2.
You take oats x2.
You light the candle before you go in.
You turn for home.
You are home.
You lay out what to take to Ford Chapel.
You set out for Ford Chapel.
A milk cart on its side, the horse dead in the traces. Crates spilled across the road.
You leave it.
Ford Chapel. A grey chapel by the old ford. The bell has not rung since.
You eat the tinned meat.
Notices for a harvest supper. Coats still on the pegs.
Foraging comes easier now. Level 1.
You go through the room slowly. You find candle x2, nails x3, scarf and work jacket.
You take scarf.
You put on the scarf.
You take candle x2.
You take nails x3.
You take work jacket.
You put on the work jacket.
The pews are full. Every head is bowed. None of them are praying.
Field guide: The unmoving.
3 of them stand here, still. None has turned.
Field guide: Listeners.
You come at the listener from behind. It goes down without a sound.
You come at the listener from behind. It goes down without a sound.
You go through the room slowly. You find ship's biscuit x3, empty bottle x4 and tinned beans.
You find a photograph: The chapel choir.
You drink the clean water.
You take ship's biscuit x3.
You take tinned beans.
You take empty bottle x4.
You put the claw hammer to the door. It goes with a crack like a shot.
A small room behind the altar. Locked from this side.
You turn the room over fast. You find ship's biscuit x2, candle x3, mill office key and spirits.
There are papers here you did not stop to read.
You take ship's biscuit x2.
You take candle x3.
You take spirits.
You take mill office key.
You light the candle before you go in.
Ladders up into the dark. The bell rope moves, a little, with no wind.
A stander stands here, still. It has not turned.
You turn for home.
You are home.
You fill 5 measures from the lock. Brown water. Boil it.
Dusk. The light goes off the river.
You feed the stove. It will burn until 22:55.
You bar the door and bank the stove for the night.
Day 2. Grey sky, low and still.
A dog sits outside the gate, thin, rope-collared, watching the door. It does not bark. It has not barked, you realise, all the time it has been there.
You put food down by the gate and step back. It eats without taking its eyes off you, then lies down by the woodpile.
You drink the clean water.
You feed the stove. It will burn until 10:02.
You haul in the night line. A fish.
Boil river water: clean water x3.
Boil river water: clean water x3.
Cook fish: cooked fish.
Make porridge: porridge x2.
Make porridge: porridge x2.
You lay out what to take to Calder Mill.
You set out for Calder Mill.
Calder Mill. Five storeys of black brick over the river. The town worked here. It is still here.
On the mill bridge, a man in a lock-keeper's waistcoat stands at the rail, looking down at the water. You know the coat. You know the set of the shoulders.
His face is calm. His eyes are open. You take the keys from his pocket because he would want you to, and you leave him looking at the river.
You eat the porridge.
The clocking-in machine. A rack of cards, every one punched for the night shift.
You go through the room slowly. You find ship's biscuit, candle x2 and tinned meat x2.
You find something written: Clocking card.
You take ship's biscuit.
You take candle x2.
You take tinned meat x2.
Machines like iron animals. The hands stand among them, white with lint.
2 of them stand here, still. None has turned.
You come at the listener from behind. It goes down without a sound.
You go through the room slowly. You find cloth x3, leather x2, machine parts x2 and scrap metal x6.
You take leather x2.
You take machine parts x2.
You take cloth x3.
You take scrap metal x6.
The key turns.
You turn for home.
You are home.
Mending comes easier now. Level 1.
Workbench: Bench with vice. Rucksacks, lamps, a hull patch.
You drink the clean water.
You fill 4 measures from the lock. Brown water. Boil it.
You feed the stove. It will burn until 20:31.
Boil river water: clean water x3.
You work along the bank and come back with firewood x2 and windfall apples.
Foraging comes easier now. Level 2.
You eat the porridge.
Dusk. The light goes off the river.
You work along the bank and come back with firewood x2 and windfall apples x2.
You bar the door and bank the stove for the night.
Day 3. Fog on the river. You cannot see the far bank.
Spoiled overnight: porridge.
The dog is still by the woodpile. It stands when you open the door and waits to see what you will do.
It eats, then walks past you into the kitchen and lies down by the stove as if it has always slept there.
You drink the clean water.
You haul in the night line. 2 fish.
You lay out what to take to The Weir.
You set out for The Weir. The dog goes ahead of you.
The Weir. Upstream, where the river falls over the stones. The widow trades on the steps.
Field guide: Running water.
Stone steps down to the water. The roar fills your head and leaves no room for anything else.
You go through the room slowly. You find yarrow and willow bark.
You take yarrow and willow bark.
A tarred hut on the sluice wall. The door hangs on one hinge.
A stander stands here, still. It has not turned.
You go through the room slowly. You find tinned beans x4.
You find something written: Weir keeper's tally.
Now you know where to find Lowe's Boatyard.
You eat the porridge.
You take tinned beans x4.
Sluice walk. The water is to your waist and it takes your breath.
A narrow iron walk over the race. Something is caught in the grating below.
You go through the room slowly. You find jerrycan, machine parts x2 and scrap metal.
You take machine parts x2.
You take scrap metal.
You turn for home.
A man face down on the towpath, a pack still on his back. He fell when it came, and he has not moved since.
You roll him to get the straps. His eyes are open.
You take bandage and satchel.
You are home. The dog drinks from the lock and lies down.
You lay out what to take to Lowe's Boatyard.
You set out for Lowe's Boatyard. The dog goes ahead of you.
Lowe's Boatyard. Sheds and slipways below the town bridge. Hulls on trestles.
A half-planked hull on the slip, its ribs open to the sky.
A stander stands here, still. It has not turned.
You drink the clean water.
You go through the room slowly. You find nails x4, pitch x2, planks x4, rope x2 and tinned beans x2.
You take tinned beans x2.
You take nails x4.
You take pitch x2.
You take rope x2.
You take planks x4.
You turn for home.
You are home. The dog drinks from the lock and lies down.
You lay out what to take to Lowe's Boatyard.
You set out for Lowe's Boatyard. The dog goes ahead of you.
You reach Lowe's Boatyard.
You go back into the slipway.
A stander stands here, still. It has not turned.
Canvas hung from the beams like washing. It moves when you do.
You go through the room slowly. You find cloth x8 and rope x2.
You find something written: Note pinned in the loft.
You take cloth x8.
You take rope x2.
You light the candle before you go in.
Benches, a cold forge, tools in their outlines on the wall.
2 of them stand here, still. None has turned.
You come at the listener from behind. It goes down without a sound.
Foraging comes easier now. Level 3.
You go through the room slowly. You find claw hammer, wharf padlock key, lamp oil, machine parts, pitch x3, bow saw and scrap metal x2.
You eat the cooked fish.
You take lamp oil.
You take claw hammer.
You take machine parts.
You take bow saw.
You take pitch x3.
You take scrap metal x2.
You take wharf padlock key.
Dry dock. The water is to your waist and it takes your breath.
The dock gates leak. Waist-deep water, black and still, and the ferry's patch on a trestle at the far end.
You turn for home.
A figure in the fog ahead, walking toward you. Walking properly, heel and toe.
It stops when you call. Then it comes much faster.
Field guide: Runners.
You hold still. They keep coming.
The runner is on you.
You hit the runner.
The dog goes in low and hangs on.
The runner turns on the dog.
You hit the runner.
The runner goes down and stays down.
It is over. The quiet comes back.
You are home. The dog drinks from the lock and lies down.
Dusk. The light goes off the river.
Workbench: Full workshop. Coil winding, a frame pack. Mending is faster.
You drink the clean water.
You feed the stove. It will burn until 02:23.
You bar the door and bank the stove for the night.
Field guide: They come to sound.
The dog wakes you, growling low at the door.
The boards give. Something is in the house.
Quiet step comes easier now. Level 1.
You do not breathe. They lose the sound of you, and stand still again.
Day 4. The sky is clear.
Spoiled overnight: raw fish.
Bare footprints in the mud around the house. They go twice round, close to the walls, and away toward the river.
You check every board twice. It costs you the morning and some nerve.
You drink the clean water.
You eat the tinned meat.
Draw nails from old boards: nails x4.
You fill 4 measures from the lock. Brown water. Boil it.
You feed the stove. It will burn until 11:51.
Boil river water: clean water x3.
Boil river water: clean water x3.
Cook fish: cooked fish.
You lay out what to take to Calder Mill.
You set out for Calder Mill. The dog goes ahead of you.
You reach Calder Mill.
You go back into the gatehouse.
The dog barks once, sharp, at nothing you can see.
You go back into the carding room.
A stander stands here, still. It has not turned.
Glass on three sides, looking down on the floor. A heavy door.
You go through the room slowly. You find ship's biscuit x2, engine house key, revolver rounds x2 and tobacco.
You find something written: Mill ledger.
Now you know where to find Coal Wharf.
You find a photograph: The new engine.
You take tobacco.
You take revolver rounds x2.
You take ship's biscuit x2.
You take engine house key.
You light the candle before you go in.
Rows of looms under a saw-tooth roof. The skylights are black with soot. You cannot see the far wall.
2 of them stand here, still. None has turned.
You drink the clean water.
You go through the room slowly. You find leather.
You take leather.
The key turns.
You light the candle before you go in.
The great engine fills the room, its flywheel taller than a house. The air hums, very low.
3 of them stand here, still. None has turned.
You go through the room slowly. You find engine belting, leather and machine parts x3.
You find something written: Engineer's log.
You take engine belting.
You take leather.
You take machine parts x3.
You turn for home.
You are home. The dog drinks from the lock and lies down.
Dusk. The light goes off the river.
You are stumbling tired.
Mending comes easier now. Level 2.
Sew a rucksack: rucksack.
You drink the clean water.
You eat the cooked fish.
You feed the stove. It will burn until 00:28.
You feed the stove. It will burn until 04:28.
You nail fresh boards over the weak places. The barricade holds at 15 of 15.
You bar the door and bank the stove for the night.
The dog wakes you, growling low at the door.
In the small hours something leans on the door, and tries it, and goes.
Day 5. The sky is clear.
You haul in the night line. A fish.
You feed the dog. It eats fast, then leans against your leg.
Cut the belting to size: drive belt.
Strip wire from old fittings: wire x2.
You lay out what to take to Coal Wharf.
You set out for Coal Wharf. The dog goes ahead of you.
Coal Wharf. Downstream, where barges load. Black heaps under a crane.
You drink the clean water.
You eat the tinned meat.
Heaps of coal slack and a line of empty carts.
A stander stands here, still. It has not turned.
You go through the room slowly. You find firewood x2 and rope x3.
You take rope x3.
A stove, two mugs, a ledger of tonnages. The kettle is dry.
A stander stands here, still. It has not turned.
You go through the room slowly. You find ship's biscuit, lamp oil, machine parts and tinned meat.
You find something written: Wharfinger's ledger.
You take ship's biscuit.
You take tinned meat.
You take lamp oil.
You take machine parts.
The dog barks once, sharp, at nothing you can see.
Barge. The water is to your waist and it takes your breath.
A coal barge half sunk at its mooring. The hold is full of water.
2 of them stand here, still. None has turned.
You go through the room slowly. You find jerrycan, rope x6 and smoked fish x5.
You take smoked fish x5.
You take rope x6.
You put the claw hammer to the door. It goes with a crack like a shot.
A brick store with a heavy padlock. Inside, drums on their sides.
You go through the room slowly. You find fuel drum and lamp oil x3.
You leave clean water here.
You leave rope x9 here.
You take fuel drum.
You take lamp oil x3.
You take clean water.
You turn for home.
You are home. The dog drinks from the lock and lies down.
Long scratches down the boards of the door, at the height of a hand, and the latch bent.
You straighten the latch and nail a batten across.
You drink the clean water.
You are stumbling tired.
Strip wire from old fittings: wire x2.
You fill 4 measures from the lock. Brown water. Boil it.
Dusk. The light goes off the river.
You work along the bank and come back with firewood x3, worms, yarrow and willow bark and windfall apples x2.
You feed the stove. It will burn until 23:13.
You bar the door and bank the stove for the night.
Three knocks on the door. Even, unhurried. Then nothing.
A woman's voice, hoarse: please, water. Only water.
Through the crack of the door: a woman, soaked to the waist, a nurse's cape over her coat. She asks for water and to sleep by your stove. She says she will be gone by morning.
She drinks, sits by the stove and sleeps sitting up. You watch her for a long time.
Day 6. Fog on the river. You cannot see the far bank.
Spoiled overnight: raw fish.
The blankets by the stove are folded. She has gone before light.
She has left a note by the stove, and a roll of bandages on top of it.
You find something written: Note left by the stove.
You drink the clean water.
You eat the tinned meat.
You lay out what to take to The Surgery.
You set out for The Surgery. The dog goes ahead of you.
The Surgery. Doctor Hale's house and surgery on Quarry Lane.
